![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070210/assets/aaa08372caf804751c80d37af49d0b27394dfe20b6d2dba6868a7739b4062921.png)

A plate with mass $M$ occupies the region $D$ enclosed between the lines $y=\frac{x}{2},$ $y=x,$ and $x=1.$ 
The mass density at each point is proportional to the square of its distance from the $y$-axis. Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the line $y=0.$
worked_solution:
The moment of inertia of a plane lamina in the shape of a region $D$ about an axis of rotation $l$ is given by

$$
{I}_{l}={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A,
$$

where $\lambda (x,y)$ is the mass density function of the lamina, and $r(x,y)$ is the distance from the line $l$ to the point $(x,y)$ on $D.$

First, notice that $D$ is a type I region with representation

$$
D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,\,\frac{x}{2}\le y\le x},
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14070210/assets/84ec89a3f4d786fe387b33aacc3de7c013866387354897f785ff69f9d65437ad.png)

Also, the distance between a point and the line $y=0$ is given by

$$
r(x,y)=|y|.
$$

Next, the mass density can be written as $\lambda (x,y)=k{x}^{2},$ where $k$ is a constant of proportionality. We can find the value of $k$ by integrating the mass density function over the plate.

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x/2}^{x}k{x}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{x/2}^{x}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{0}^{1}{[{x}^{2}y]}_{x/2}^{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{0}^{1}({x}^{3}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{2})\,\text{d}x \\  & =k{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{{x}^{3}}{2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =k\cdot {[\frac{{x}^{4}}{8}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{k}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, 

$$
\lambda (x,y)=k{x}^{2}=8M{x}^{2}.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the line $y=0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{l} & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)[r(x,y)]^{2}\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x/2}^{x}8M{x}^{2}{y}^{2}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & =8M{\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{{x}^{2}{y}^{3}}{3}]}_{x/2}^{x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =8M{\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{{x}^{5}}{3}-\frac{{x}^{5}}{24})\,\text{d}x \\  & =8M{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{7{x}^{5}}{24}\,\text{d}x \\  & =M{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{7{x}^{5}}{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =M{[\frac{7{x}^{6}}{18}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{7M}{18}.\end{aligned}
$$
